subject: general
question: According to the 2024 Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) findings, how does corruption most directly undermine global climate action?

options.text: By weakening financial markets in developing countries
By discouraging public participation in environmental protests
By diverting climate funds and allowing undue influence over environmental policies
By increasing competition among fossil fuel companies

solution:
The correct answer is __**By diverting climate funds and allowing undue influence over environmental policies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Corruption diverts funds allocated for climate change mitigation and adaptation projects, reducing their effectiveness and delaying critical climate action.
 
• By allowing undue influence over environmental policies, corrupt practices prioritize the interests of powerful corporations or individuals over the environment and public welfare.
 
• Mismanagement of climate funds can lead to inefficient or poorly executed projects, further exacerbating environmental degradation.
 
• Corruption undermines trust in public institutions and international climate agreements, discouraging investment and collaboration in environmental initiatives.
 
• According to Transparency International, corruption in environmental governance is a significant barrier to achieving global climate goals, as it weakens enforcement mechanisms and promotes unsustainable practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Corruption and Global Climate Action**

 
 
• Corruption poses a significant challenge to global efforts to combat climate change, as it weakens the governance and implementation of policies.
 
• Addressing corruption is crucial for ensuring the effective use of climate funds and achieving sustainable development goals (SDGs).
 
• Global initiatives, such as the Paris Agreement, emphasize the need for transparency and accountability in climate financing and governance.
